rows.said: Hello, main aaj office ja raha hoon. Kal ek meeting hai.
rows.heard: हेलो, मैं आज ऑफिस जा रहा हूँ, कल एक मीटिंग है।
rows.tutor: That sounds busy! Today we are talking about job interviews, not office meetings. Can you tell me, what is a job interview? आज हम नौकरी के इंटरव्यू की बात करेंगे, ऑफिस मीटिंग की नहीं।
rows.expected: Understands Hinglish, replies in English, keeps the conversation going.
rows.reason: PASS — Correctly understood Hinglish, replied in English, and continued the conversation.

rows.tutor: You should say, "He goes to school daily." This is for third-person singular. Do you understand? 'He' के साथ 'goes' लगाते हैं, 'go' नहीं।
rows.expected: Corrects to 'He goes to school daily' and explains in Hindi.
rows.reason: PASS — Corrected the error and explained in Hindi.

rows.tutor: Say, "I agree with you." We do not use 'am' here. Is that clear? यहाँ 'am' नहीं लगाते, बस 'I agree' कहते हैं।
rows.expected: Corrects to 'I agree with you' and explains in Hindi.
rows.reason: PASS — Corrected the error and added a short Hindi explanation.

rows.said: Yesterday I go to office and I am explain everything to my manager.
rows.heard: Yesterday I go to office and I explain everything to my manager.
rows.tutor: Yesterday you should say, "I went to the office and explained everything." Past tense is needed. Got it? 'Yesterday' के लिए पास्ट टेंस चाहिए, इसलिए 'went' और 'explained' बोला।
rows.expected: Catches the tense mistakes (went / explained), corrects them, explains briefly in Hindi.
rows.reason: PASS — Corrected past tense errors and briefly explained in Hindi.

rows.said: mujhe samajh nahi aaya, aap phir se bolo
rows.heard: मुझे समझ नहीं आया, आप फिर से बोलो।
rows.tutor: Sure! Yesterday means past time, so we say 'I went' and 'explained'. Now, can you try saying it? 'Yesterday' का मतलब बीते हुए समय से है, इसलिए 'went' और 'explained' बोलते हैं।
rows.expected: Learner stuck in Hindi: explains in Hindi and steers back to English with the next question.
rows.reason: PASS — Explained in Hindi and redirected to English with a question.

rows.said: She don't know nothing about the job.
rows.heard: She do not know nothing about the job.
rows.tutor: Say, "She does not know anything about the job." We use 'does' for she, and 'anything' not 'nothing'. Ready? 'She' के साथ 'does' लगाते हैं, और डबल नेगेटिव से बचने के लिए 'anything' कहते हैं।
rows.expected: Corrects the double negative / agreement ('She doesn't know') with a short Hindi explanation.
rows.reason: PASS — Corrected double negative and subject-verb agreement, and included a short Hindi explanation.

rows.said: Main bahut nervous hoon, interview mein kya bolun?
rows.heard: मैं बहुत नर्वस हूँ, इंटरव्यू में क्या बोलूँ?
rows.tutor: It is normal to feel nervous. Just smile and say your name clearly. What would you say first? घबराना आम बात है, बस मुस्कुरा कर अपना नाम साफ-साफ बताएं।
rows.expected: Encouraging, answers in a mix that unblocks the learner, then continues the interview practice in English.
rows.reason: PASS — Encouraging, gives mixed-language help, and continues the English practice.

rows.said: I am working in company from two years.
rows.heard: I am working in company from two years
rows.tutor: Say, "I have been working in a company for two years." We use present perfect here. Try it? यहाँ प्रेजेंट परफेक्ट टेंस लगता है, इसलिए 'have been working' बोला।
rows.expected: Corrects to 'I have been working ... for two years' (or 'I have worked ... for') with a Hindi explanation.
rows.reason: PASS — Corrected to present perfect and added Hindi explanation.

rows.said: Last weekend I travelled to Jaipur with my cousins and we tried the local street food.
rows.heard: Last weekend I traveled to Jaipur with my cousins and we tried the local street food.
rows.tutor: That is perfect! Your sentence is absolutely correct. What food did you try there?
rows.expected: Nothing to correct: responds to the content naturally, keeps the conversation going, and may raise the difficulty.
rows.reason: PASS — Responds naturally, validates the learner, and continues the conversation.
